## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Catutthapāṭidesanīya* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya 4) is the fourth and final rule in the *pāṭidesanīya* (offenses requiring confession) section of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. As classified within the broader Pātimokkha structure, the *pāṭidesaniya* category comprises four rules for fully ordained monks, the infringement of which requires formal acknowledgement and confession [von Hinüber 1996]. The regulation concerns forest dwellings: a monk who accepts food in a hazardous wilderness lodging without prior notice must acknowledge the offense [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate wide cross-tradition preservation, matching the rule in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as the corresponding fourth *pāṭidesanīya* rules preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya traditions (including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya recensions) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also registers an internal passage parallel with *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 29 [SuttaCentral]. Computed text reuse in DharmaNexus detects extensive shared phrasing with other Vinaya texts, particularly *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya* 3, the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, Khandhaka chapters (Kd 1, Kd 15, and Kd 18), and multiple *Pācittiya* rules, alongside cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Prātimokṣasūtra* and the Tibetan *Vinayasūtravṛtti* [DharmaNexus].

Apart from Oskar von Hinüber's structural overview listing the four *pāṭidesaniya* rules in the Vinaya [von Hinüber 1996], the secondary literature search yielded no direct discussions, returning only homonymous citations of other non-Vinaya texts.
